newsitem.title: USA: Poor communications blamed in cruise fire in Alaska.
newsitem.headline: Poor communications blamed in cruise fire in Alaska.

text.p: Communications problems hampered rescue efforts when a fire broke out on a cruise ship plying Alaska's Inside Passage last summer, according to a U.S. Coast Guard report issued on Monday.

Fire control plans and procedures aboard the Universe Explorer, a Panamanian-flagged ship operated by World Explorer Cruises, were also faulted in the report, prepared by the Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in Juneau.

The July 27 blaze started in the laundry room of the ship as it headed for Glacier Bay from Juneau. Five crew members were killed by smoke inhalation and 73 other people, mostly crew members, were injured. The cruise was cancelled, and passengers were evacuated and flown home.
The report's findings and recommendations will be sent to the cruise ship industry and the National Transportation Safety Board, which is still conducting its investigation, the Coast Guard said.
Fire teams were unable to communicate with each other, except face to face, because hand-held radios failed to operate inside the ship's superstructure, the report said.
Particularly at risk were crew members trapped in their cabins by smoke, the report said.
"As they had no other way of communicating their distress, they had to wait until they heard rescuers in the passageway, then they pounded on the door to attract attention," it said.

Fire-screen doors closed too late, allowing smoke to spread through the ship and outdated fire-control plans did not take into account 1991 alterations which removed a bulkhead from the laundry room, the report said.

The report also criticised as inadequate an at-sea emergency drill four days before the fire, saying passengers were allowed to use elevators and other escape routes that were out of bounds during the real emergency.
